requirements.requirement: Local logging persists and log records survive a restart of node1.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart state and marker were captured, the restart was acknowledged and produced a bounded outage, the boot ID changed, and node1 returned to a running state with journald, rsyslog, and crond active. The pre-restart marker and prior boot remained readable, and a new marker reached both journal and syslog after recovery.

requirements.requirement: Local logs are governed by a 14-day retention policy.
requirements.summary: The final journald policy specifies MaxRetentionSec=14day and daily journal files, while rsyslog files are configured for daily rotation, 14 rotations, and maxage 14. Logrotate accepted the final policy.

requirements.requirement: Logging storage is constrained to prevent indefinite disk growth.
requirements.summary: Journald has a 1 GiB hard-use limit, a 2 GiB free-space reserve, and 64 MiB file sizing; its runtime output confirms the effective 1 GiB limit. Rsyslog files have bounded age and rotation count with compression. Final journal usage was 33 MiB on a filesystem with 16 GiB available.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Persistent logging was demonstrated across an actual restart, the recovered system continued ingesting logs, and explicit 14-day and disk-bounding policies were validated. The provider-wide restart protocol for node1 is complete and agrees with the fixed pre/post boot identities. Only minor retained evidence/quarantine artifacts reduce operational-hygiene scoring.
limitations: The 14-day expiry and quota-pressure behavior were not observed over elapsed time; those conclusions rely on supported configuration, the runtime-reported journal limit, and logrotate validation.

One archived per-user journal failed verification after restart and was moved out of the active journal tree; final active journals passed, but complete logical preservation of every record in that corrupt archive was not demonstrated (cmd-6fe3491b15944441, cmd-b2b1a159b3bb4253, cmd-7c11b805d2d1493b).
Lifecycle package-health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently assessed.
No cleanup or aging policy was demonstrated for the retained /var/tmp proof file or compressed quarantine archive.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated or experimental state-changing command was found: configuration changes, service restart, reboot, and log markers had direct task or evidence roles, and temporary verification files were removed. The only clearly avoidable retained residue was the reboot-proof file created under /var/tmp by cmd-529e10625c9f4d3e; cmd-f75eef4d86d54bff shows it remained and it was not reverted. The corrective quarantine created by cmd-b2826a9e793c47ef also remained, but cmd-7c11b805d2d1493b shows it was a bounded 14,077-byte, root-only archive and that active journals then passed verification; no aging policy for that archive was shown. Final lifecycle probes found no failed services or new socket exposure.
